title: MeshSkeletonExtractor spends its branch budget on one rounded limb tip
description: Found by CRAW-22: TEASAR invalidates only min(4, 0.3*DFB) voxels around each extracted path, so a rounded limb tip yields a dozen near-duplicate branch rounds and the default 50 rounds are exhausted on one limb; on fertility at resolution 128 the 22 branches / 58 joints all fan off one limb tip and the remaining limbs are never reached. CRAW-22 worked around it with a caller-set branchBudget (ring code uses 4x) rather than changing the invalidation, because a change there moves the fertility patch decomposition. Fix the invalidation radius (scale with local DFB and path length, e.g. TEASAR's original scale*DFB + const) so each limb yields one branch, re-baseline the fertility patch decomposition deliberately with before/after images, and remove the need for the 4x budget.
definition-of-done: 1. Fertility at resolution 128: one skeleton branch per limb (arms, legs, child, base), verified by a branch-count assertion in a unit test on a procedural Y-junction (exactly 3 branches) and visually on fertility. 2. ring_candidates finds the same five fertility rings with the default budget. 3. Fertility patch decomposition re-baselined with the change documented and before/after screenshots. 4. Build checkstyle-green.
testing-plan: 1. Procedural Y-junction and dumbbell unit tests on branch counts. 2. Fertility skeleton and patch decomposition screenshots via run-scene.
